exams.name: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement processes and communications
questions.subdomain: Design and implement traceability and flow of work
questions.question: A team wants every commit and pull request to be traceable to a work item in Azure Boards. What should they do?
options: Mention work item IDs in commits and pull requests, such as AB#123 in GitHub or #123 in Azure Repos, and require linked work items in branch policies
Keep a spreadsheet of commits and work items
Use only email to report progress
Create one work item for the whole year
questions.correct_rationale: Linking commits and PRs to work items gives end-to-end traceability, and branch policies can enforce it.
questions.distractor_summary: Spreadsheets and email are manual, and one giant work item gives no traceability.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement processes and communications
questions.subdomain: Design and implement traceability and flow of work
questions.question: What does a Kanban board's work-in-progress (WIP) limit do?
options: It limits the number of team members
It restricts who can create work items
It caps how many items can be in a column at once to expose bottlenecks and improve flow
questions.correct_rationale: WIP limits keep teams from starting too much at once and reveal where work piles up.
questions.distractor_summary: WIP limits do not control team size, sprint length, or permissions.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement processes and communications
questions.subdomain: Design and implement traceability and flow of work
questions.question: A product owner wants to see how long work items take from start to finish. Which metric fits?
questions.correct_rationale: Cycle time measures how long items take once work starts.
questions.distractor_summary: Velocity is work completed per sprint, coverage measures tests, and MTTR measures recovery.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement processes and communications
questions.subdomain: Design and implement traceability and flow of work
questions.question: What is the difference between lead time and cycle time?
options: Lead time is from when an item is created to when it is done, while cycle time starts when work begins
Cycle time includes time waiting in the backlog
questions.correct_rationale: Lead time includes backlog wait, while cycle time measures active work.
questions.distractor_summary: They differ, cycle time excludes backlog wait, and lead time is not about builds.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement processes and communications
questions.subdomain: Design and implement traceability and flow of work
questions.question: A company uses GitHub for code and Azure Boards for planning. How can they link the two for traceability?
options: Install the Azure Boards app for GitHub and connect repositories to the Azure DevOps project
Move all code into Azure Repos first
questions.correct_rationale: The Azure Boards app connects GitHub commits, PRs, and issues to work items.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual copying is error-prone, moving code is unnecessary, and wikis do not link work.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement processes and communications
questions.subdomain: Design and implement traceability and flow of work
questions.question: Which Azure Boards view shows features and epics across several sprints and teams on a timeline?
questions.correct_rationale: Delivery Plans show work across teams and iterations.
questions.distractor_summary: PRs, build summaries, and feeds are not planning views.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement processes and communications
questions.subdomain: Design and implement traceability and flow of work
questions.question: A team wants GitHub issues to move automatically between columns as pull requests open and merge. What should they use?
options: Manual updates by the team lead only
A branch policy in Azure Repos
GitHub Projects with built-in workflows or GitHub Actions automation
questions.correct_rationale: GitHub Projects workflows can update item status when PRs change.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual updates are slow, and Artifacts and Azure Repos branch policies do not move GitHub project items.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions

questions.subdomain: Design and implement traceability and flow of work
questions.question: What is the purpose of a value stream map in DevOps?
options: To visualize the steps from idea to delivery and find waste and delays
questions.correct_rationale: Value stream maps show flow and wait times across the delivery process.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not track hours, design schemas, or store artifacts.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 1. Design and implement processes and communications
questions.subdomain: Design and implement traceability and flow of work
questions.question: Work items are being closed without code changes reviewed. Leaders want to make sure PRs that close work items pass review first. What should be configured?
options: Branch policies requiring reviewers and linked work items, with completion of the PR resolving the work items
Use a single administrator to close all items
questions.correct_rationale: Branch policies and PR completion options tie reviews to work item closure.
questions.distractor_summary: Direct pushes bypass reviews, disabling links removes traceability, and one person closing items does not enforce review.

questions.correct_rationale: Deployment frequency is one of the four key delivery metrics.

The number of commits per day
The time it takes to build code
questions.correct_rationale: Change failure rate tracks how often changes cause incidents or rollbacks.

The Azure DevOps or GitHub app for Teams with subscriptions to the relevant events

questions.distractor_summary: Manual emails and spreadsheets are slow, and WIP limits are unrelated.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions

questions.question: Release notes must be generated automatically from merged pull requests between two tags in GitHub. What fits?
options: Writing notes by hand from memory
GitHub's automatically generated release notes, configured with a release.yml file
A wiki page with no links
questions.correct_rationale: GitHub can build release notes from PRs and labels between releases.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual notes and unrelated exports miss changes.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.subdomain: Plan and implement branching strategies for the source code
questions.question: What is trunk-based development?
options: Every feature lives on a long-lived branch for months
Developers integrate small changes into a single main branch frequently, using short-lived branches and feature flags
Each developer has a permanent personal branch
Code is only merged once a year
questions.correct_rationale: Trunk-based development keeps branches short and integration continuous.
questions.distractor_summary: Long-lived branches and rare merges are the opposite of trunk-based development.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions

questions.question: A team wants hidden features in production that can be enabled later without redeploying. What should they use?
options: Feature flags, for example with Azure App Configuration feature management
A new repository for each feature
questions.correct_rationale: Feature flags separate deployment from release.
questions.distractor_summary: Long branches delay integration, separate repos fragment code, and hotfixes do not hide features.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.subdomain: Plan and implement branching strategies for the source code
questions.question: Pull requests to main must have at least two reviewers, a successful build, and resolved comments. What should be configured in Azure Repos?
options: A rule in the team wiki
Branch policies on main for minimum reviewers, build validation, and comment resolution
questions.correct_rationale: Branch policies enforce review and quality gates before merging.
questions.distractor_summary: Wiki rules are not enforced, forks do not gate merges, and retention policies manage data.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design and implement a source control strategy

questions.question: In GitHub, which feature enforces required status checks and reviews before merging to a branch?
options: Branch protection rules or repository rulesets
questions.correct_rationale: Branch protection and rulesets require checks and reviews on protected branches.
questions.distractor_summary: Pages, templates, and Discussions do not gate merges.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.subdomain: Plan and implement branching strategies for the source code
questions.question: Which merge strategy combines all commits of a PR into one commit on the target branch?
questions.correct_rationale: Squash merge creates a single commit containing all changes.
questions.distractor_summary: The other strategies keep individual commits.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.subdomain: Plan and implement branching strategies for the source code
questions.question: A team needs to maintain version 1.x with bug fixes while developing 2.0 on main. Which branching approach fits?
options: Develop everything on a single branch with no tags
Create a release branch for 1.x, fix bugs there, and cherry-pick or merge fixes to main as needed
Delete main and work only on 1.x
Fork the repository into a new organization
questions.correct_rationale: Release branches support maintenance of older versions alongside new work.
questions.distractor_summary: A single branch cannot ship two versions, deleting main breaks development, and forks split history.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.subdomain: Plan and implement branching strategies for the source code
questions.question: Which file lists required reviewers for parts of a GitHub repository based on file paths?
questions.correct_rationale: CODEOWNERS requests reviews from owners automatically.
questions.distractor_summary: README describes the project, .gitignore excludes files, and LICENSE sets terms.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.subdomain: Plan and implement branching strategies for the source code
questions.question: Developers must not push directly to main, even administrators. What should be enabled?
options: Branch protection that applies to administrators, or a ruleset with no bypass list
A wiki page explaining the rule
questions.correct_rationale: Including administrators in protection or rulesets blocks direct pushes for everyone.
questions.distractor_summary: Quotas, LFS, and documentation do not enforce restrictions.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.subdomain: Plan and implement branching strategies for the source code
questions.question: What does GitFlow use in addition to main?
options: A develop branch plus feature, release, and hotfix branches
questions.correct_rationale: GitFlow uses develop and supporting branch types.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not single-branch, per-developer, or branchless.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions

questions.subdomain: Plan and implement branching strategies for the source code
questions.question: A PR needs build validation that only runs when files in a specific folder change. What should be configured in Azure Repos?
options: A required reviewer for every file
A retention policy for the folder
A build validation policy with a path filter
A separate repository for that folder
questions.correct_rationale: Path filters run validation only when matching files change.
questions.distractor_summary: Reviewers, retention, and separate repos do not filter build triggers.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions

questions.question: Commits must be proven to come from verified authors. What should be required on GitHub?
options: Signed commits, with branch protection requiring signatures
questions.correct_rationale: Signed commits verify the author with GPG, SSH, or S/MIME signatures.
questions.distractor_summary: Message length, merge type, and LFS do not verify identity.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions

questions.subdomain: Plan and implement branching strategies for the source code

questions.correct_rationale: Cherry-pick copies a commit to another branch.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions

options: A feature flag with a percentage or targeting filter, monitored through telemetry
A long-lived branch deployed to 10 percent of servers manually
questions.correct_rationale: Percentage filters gradually expose features while telemetry confirms health.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual branch deployments are error-prone, and repos or hotfix branches do not target users.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions

questions.question: What is a .gitignore file used for?
options: Telling Git which files and folders not to track, such as build outputs
questions.correct_rationale: .gitignore prevents unwanted files from being committed.
questions.distractor_summary: CODEOWNERS lists owners, pipeline YAML defines steps, and secrets do not belong in repos.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.subdomain: Design and implement and manage repositories
questions.question: A secret was committed to a repository and pushed. What is the correct response?
options: Delete the file in a new commit and do nothing else
Make the repository private and keep the secret
Revoke and rotate the secret immediately, then remove it from history with a tool such as git filter-repo, and enable push protection
questions.correct_rationale: The exposed secret must be rotated because history keeps it, and cleanup plus push protection prevent repeats.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting the file leaves it in history, privacy does not make it safe, and renaming changes nothing.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.subdomain: Design and implement and manage repositories
questions.question: Which GitHub feature blocks pushes that contain known secret patterns?
questions.correct_rationale: Push protection rejects pushes with detected secrets.
questions.distractor_summary: Dependabot updates packages, Pages hosts sites, and issue forms structure issues.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.subdomain: Design and implement and manage repositories
questions.question: A monolithic repository must be split, keeping each folder's history. What can help?
options: git subtree split or git filter-repo to extract folders with history
Copy files into new repos without history
questions.correct_rationale: These tools rewrite history to keep only the chosen paths.
questions.distractor_summary: Copying loses history, forks keep everything, and deletion loses everything.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design and implement a source control strategy
questions.subdomain: Design and implement and manage repositories
questions.question: What is Scalar used for with Git?
options: Improving performance for very large repositories with features such as background maintenance and partial clone
questions.correct_rationale: Scalar configures Git for large repos.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not for packages, pipelines, or work items.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions

questions.question: A team must move a repository from another Git host to Azure Repos with all history and branches. What should they do?

Use the Import repository feature or push a mirror clone to the new remote

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 2. Design and implement a source control strategy

options: Branch creation permissions on the repository combined with allowed folder patterns, such as feature/*
questions.correct_rationale: Repo permissions can restrict branch creation to specific namespaces.
questions.distractor_summary: Retention, wikis, and upstream sources do not control branch creation.

questions.question: An Azure Pipeline must deploy to Azure without storing a client secret. What should be used for the service connection?
options: A personal access token of an administrator
Workload identity federation with a Microsoft Entra app or managed identity
A client secret with no expiry

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 4. Develop a security and compliance plan
questions.subdomain: Design and implement authentication and authorization methods
questions.question: A GitHub Actions workflow must deploy to Azure without storing secrets in GitHub. What should be configured?

A repository secret with an admin password
A public repository variable with the client secret
An SSH key stored in the workflow file
questions.correct_rationale: OIDC exchanges a short-lived GitHub token for an Azure access token.
questions.distractor_summary: Stored passwords and keys in files are insecure.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 4. Develop a security and compliance plan

questions.question: What is a personal access token in Azure DevOps?
options: A token that grants a user's access to Azure DevOps with chosen scopes and an expiry
questions.correct_rationale: PATs authenticate tools and scripts on behalf of a user.
questions.distractor_summary: They are not artifacts, policies, or variable groups.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 4. Develop a security and compliance plan
questions.subdomain: Design and implement authentication and authorization methods
questions.question: A pipeline must be allowed to deploy to production only after a release manager approves. What should be configured?
options: An approval check on the production environment
questions.correct_rationale: Environment checks pause deployments until approvers sign off.
questions.distractor_summary: Agent pools, wikis, and retention do not gate deployments.

questions.question: Which Azure DevOps security group can manage all project settings?
questions.correct_rationale: Project Administrators manage project-level settings and permissions.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 4. Develop a security and compliance plan
questions.subdomain: Design and implement a strategy for managing sensitive information in automation
questions.question: How do secret variables behave in Azure Pipelines logs?
options: They are masked in logs and are not passed to scripts as environment variables unless mapped explicitly
They are printed in clear text
They are stored in Git history
They can be read by anyone with the pipeline URL
questions.correct_rationale: Secret variables are encrypted, masked, and must be mapped explicitly into scripts.
questions.distractor_summary: They are not printed, committed, or public.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 4. Develop a security and compliance plan
questions.subdomain: Design and implement a strategy for managing sensitive information in automation
questions.question: A workflow must use a secret only in the production deployment job, and only after approval. What fits in GitHub?
options: A repository secret available to all jobs
An organization variable visible to all repos
A secret in the workflow file
An environment secret on a protected production environment with required reviewers
questions.correct_rationale: Environment secrets are only released to jobs that pass the environment's protection rules.
questions.distractor_summary: Repository and organization values are broader, and files expose secrets.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 4. Develop a security and compliance plan
questions.subdomain: Design and implement a strategy for managing sensitive information in automation
questions.question: What is a secure file in Azure Pipelines?
options: A file committed to the main branch
A file such as a certificate or signing key stored encrypted in the library and downloaded during a pipeline run
questions.correct_rationale: Secure files store sensitive files outside the repo for pipeline use.
questions.distractor_summary: Committed files, wiki attachments, and test results are not secured this way.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 4. Develop a security and compliance plan
questions.subdomain: Design and implement a strategy for managing sensitive information in automation
questions.question: Applications must read configuration and secrets at run time without storing them in code. What should be used?
options: Azure App Configuration with Key Vault references and managed identities
questions.correct_rationale: App Configuration and Key Vault keep settings and secrets outside code.
questions.distractor_summary: Committed and hard-coded values leak, and comments are not configuration.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 4. Develop a security and compliance plan
questions.subdomain: Automate security and compliance scanning
questions.question: A team wants to find vulnerable open source dependencies in its GitHub repos and get pull requests that update them. What should be enabled?
questions.correct_rationale: Dependabot detects vulnerable dependencies and opens update PRs.
questions.distractor_summary: Pages hosts sites, LFS stores files, and branch protection does not scan dependencies.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions

questions.subdomain: Automate security and compliance scanning
questions.question: What does CodeQL do in GitHub Advanced Security?

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions

Use pull_request_target and check out the PR head with secrets available

Releasing a new version to a small subset of users or servers first, then expanding if it is healthy

Deployments must always delete resources first
questions.correct_rationale: Idempotent deployments converge to the desired state.
questions.distractor_summary: Idempotence avoids duplicates and repeated deletion and allows reapplying.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Design and implement infrastructure as code (IaC)
questions.question: A Bicep deployment must create resources in a resource group and also assign a policy at the subscription level. What should be used?
options: A deployment with targetScope set appropriately and modules scoped to the resource group and subscription
A single resource group deployment for both
An ARM template with no scopes
questions.correct_rationale: Bicep supports deployments at different scopes using targetScope and module scopes.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual steps lose automation, and resource group deployments cannot assign subscription-level policy alone.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Design and implement infrastructure as code (IaC)
questions.question: Which tool runs desired state configuration for Linux and Windows machines through playbooks?
questions.correct_rationale: Ansible uses playbooks to configure machines.
questions.distractor_summary: Boards, Discussions, and Test Plans do not configure machines.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Design and implement infrastructure as code (IaC)
questions.question: A team wants to test Terraform modules automatically before publishing them. What practice fits?
options: Run terraform validate, fmt checks, and terraform test in a CI pipeline
questions.correct_rationale: Automated checks catch module errors early.
questions.distractor_summary: Untested publishing, production testing, and bug reports are late and risky.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Maintain pipelines
questions.question: Pipeline runs are slow because dependencies are downloaded every time. What should be added?
options: A cache step for the package manager's dependency folder, keyed on the lock file
questions.correct_rationale: Caching dependencies based on lock files speeds up builds.
questions.distractor_summary: More stages, bigger repos, and approvals do not speed up downloads.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Maintain pipelines
questions.question: What does a retention policy do in Azure Pipelines?
options: Controls how long pipeline runs, logs, and artifacts are kept
questions.correct_rationale: Retention settings limit how long run data is stored.
questions.distractor_summary: Approvals, package retention, and branch names are separate settings.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Maintain pipelines
questions.question: Old classic release pipelines must be migrated to YAML. What is a reasonable approach?
options: Recreate the stages as YAML deployment jobs with environments and checks, test them side by side, then retire the classic pipeline
Delete the classic pipelines and start over without testing
Export the classic pipeline as YAML and deploy it without review
Keep both forever with no plan
questions.correct_rationale: Rebuilding as YAML with environments and testing keeps deployments safe during migration.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting without testing is risky, exports need review, and running both forever is waste.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Maintain pipelines
questions.question: Which metric helps identify whether pipeline failures are caused by infrastructure or by code?
options: The pipeline failure report grouped by task and error type
questions.correct_rationale: Failure reports show where and why runs fail.
questions.distractor_summary: Velocity, burndown, and downloads do not explain failures.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Maintain pipelines
questions.question: Pipeline jobs queue for a long time before starting. What could reduce waiting?
options: Purchase more parallel jobs or add more self-hosted agents
questions.correct_rationale: More concurrency reduces queue time.
questions.distractor_summary: Stages, retention, and approvals do not add capacity.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Maintain pipelines
questions.question: An organization wants to stop pipelines from using unapproved tasks and running arbitrary scripts. What should be configured?
options: Organization pipeline settings to limit tasks and require templates, with checks that enforce extends templates
questions.correct_rationale: Settings and required templates restrict what pipelines can run.
questions.distractor_summary: Agents, retention, and branches do not restrict pipeline content.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Maintain pipelines
questions.question: A pipeline intermittently fails when calling an external service. What is a practical improvement?
options: Add retries with backoff for the task, and investigate the dependency's availability
questions.correct_rationale: Retries handle brief failures while root causes are investigated.
questions.distractor_summary: Removing steps, hiding errors, and running less often do not fix reliability.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Maintain pipelines
questions.question: In Azure Pipelines, what does retryCountOnTaskFailure do?
options: Retries a failed task a set number of times before failing the job
Retries an entire pipeline after a day
questions.correct_rationale: The setting reruns failed tasks automatically.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not retry pipelines, reviews, or approvals.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Maintain pipelines
questions.question: Self-hosted agents must keep up to date with patches and tools. What approach reduces maintenance?
options: Patch each agent manually when someone remembers
Share admin passwords to all developers
Build agent images with infrastructure as code and use ephemeral agents that are replaced regularly
questions.correct_rationale: Image pipelines and ephemeral agents keep agents current and consistent.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual patching is unreliable, never updating is insecure, and shared passwords are risky.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Maintain pipelines
questions.question: What is the effect of setting the timeoutInMinutes property on a job?
options: The job waits that long before starting
The job runs every that many minutes
The job's logs are kept that long
The job is cancelled if it runs longer than the specified time
questions.correct_rationale: Timeouts stop runaway jobs.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not delay, schedule, or retain logs.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Maintain pipelines
questions.question: A pipeline produces large artifacts that consume storage. What is a good maintenance step?
options: Set retention to keep only the needed runs and artifacts, and remove unneeded outputs from publishing
questions.correct_rationale: Retention and smaller artifacts control storage use.
questions.distractor_summary: Keeping everything, publishing whole disks, and committing artifacts waste storage.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Maintain pipelines
questions.question: What does the Azure Pipelines agent pool maintenance feature do for self-hosted pools?
options: It cleans up working directories and repository state on agents on a schedule
questions.correct_rationale: Maintenance jobs free disk space by cleaning agent folders.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not create projects, merge PRs, or delete pools.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Maintain pipelines
questions.question: The team wants to know which pipelines use a deprecated task so it can update them. What is the most efficient approach?
options: Search the repositories for the task name in YAML files, and review usage reported in the organization settings
questions.correct_rationale: Searching code finds all YAML references quickly.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual review is slow, waiting causes outages, and chat is unreliable.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Maintain pipelines
questions.question: What does the Dependabot version updates feature do for GitHub Actions workflows?
options: Opens pull requests to update the versions of actions used in workflows
questions.correct_rationale: Dependabot can keep action versions current.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not delete workflows, change runners, or approve deployments.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Maintain pipelines
questions.question: Actions in workflows are referenced by tag, and the team worries a tag could be moved to malicious code. What is safer?
options: Use the latest branch for every action
Pin third-party actions to a full-length commit SHA
questions.correct_rationale: SHA pinning makes the reference immutable.
questions.distractor_summary: Branches and unversioned references can change, and wikis do not run actions.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Design and implement a package management strategy
questions.question: A company wants developers to get npm packages only through its Azure Artifacts feed so that every public package is cached and reviewed. What should be configured?
options: Direct access to the public registry from every machine
A Git submodule for each package
An .npmrc that points the registry to the feed, with npmjs added as an upstream source
A wiki list of approved packages
questions.correct_rationale: Routing installs through the feed caches packages and gives one control point.
questions.distractor_summary: Direct access skips the feed, submodules are not package management, and a list does not enforce anything.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Design and implement a testing strategy for pipelines
questions.question: What is the main purpose of integration tests?
options: Checking a single function in isolation
Checking that components work together correctly, such as an app with its database or another service
questions.correct_rationale: Integration tests cover how parts interact.
questions.distractor_summary: Unit tests isolate functions, linters check formatting, and cost is unrelated.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Design and implement deployments
questions.question: A release must go to a staging environment first, and production must use exactly the same artifact. How should the pipeline be designed?
options: Separate pipelines that each build from source
One multi-stage pipeline that builds once, publishes an artifact, and deploys it to staging and then production
Copy files manually from staging to production
Deploy production first and staging later
questions.correct_rationale: Multi-stage pipelines promote the same artifact through environments.
questions.distractor_summary: Rebuilding risks differences, manual copying is error-prone, and the order is reversed in the last choice.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Design and implement infrastructure as code (IaC)
questions.question: Which Terraform command shows the changes that will be made without applying them?
questions.correct_rationale: plan previews changes, while apply makes them.
questions.distractor_summary: apply and destroy change infrastructure, and fmt formats code.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Maintain pipelines
questions.question: Pipeline secrets in a variable group are about to expire. What practice prevents outages?
options: Wait for pipelines to fail, then update
Set secrets to never expire in plain text variables
Store backup secrets in the repository
Store secrets in Key Vault with expiry alerts and rotate them before they expire, using the linked variable group
questions.correct_rationale: Key Vault expiry monitoring and rotation avoid surprise failures.
questions.distractor_summary: Waiting causes outages, plain text is insecure, and repos must not hold secrets.

questions.exam: Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions
questions.domain: 3. Design and implement build and release pipelines
questions.subdomain: Design and implement pipelines
questions.question: Which GitHub Actions runner type is maintained by GitHub and gives a fresh VM for each job?
questions.correct_rationale: GitHub-hosted runners provide clean VMs maintained by GitHub.
questions.distractor_summary: Self-hosted runners are maintained by you, runner groups organize runners, and Codespaces are dev environments.
